characters.name: Rokuro "Rock" Okajima
characters.description: A former JapaneseSalaryman, Rokuro "Rock" Okajima serves as the the Lagoon Company's negotiator and translator, and is the series' primary POV Character. Although the least physically dangerous member of the Company, Rock possesses the ability to negotiate withheavily-armed,insane,hyper-violentindividuals; he not only gets out of such negotiations alive, but even convinces them to see things his way. Action Survivor: He's survived being caught in the middle of multiple gunfights, being kidnapped several times, a collapsing building, boat chases, car chases, assaults from various ultra-violent maniacs… and Revy. Adaptational Heroism: In the manga, Rock's motivation in "Baile de la Muerte" are mostly forgigglesand to win a bet with Chang. In the OVA, rather than a bet with Chang, he's actively trying to break the cycle of crime and violence in Roanapur by cutting the gangs off at their source: the drug trade coming through the Golden Triangle. It's also indicated he's much more driven to help Garcia and Roberta by his failure to save Yukio. To still show he's going down a dark road, by the tail end of the arc Rock is relishing his planning and manipulation of events almost to the equivalent of Revy when she's shooting people. All-Loving Hero: At first, that's what he tried to do. He tried to keep violence down, respect the dead and even save nutjobs like Hansel and Gretel. Amazon Chaser: While is unknown if it's romantic on his part, he's close to Revy, a violent and dangerous female criminal. When he saw her take out two boats of hostiles in the first arc, he was in awe of her; she's definitely got a thing for him however.

characters.name: Rebecca "Revy" Lee
characters.description: A nihilistic Chinese-American gunwoman and the Lagoon Company's primary muscle. Known as "Two Hands" after her preferredstyle of shooting.Her first name is apparently "Rebecca", but nothing more is known of her past apart from the implication that it wasn't a happy one. '90s Anti-Hero: She has a rough but cool name, a nihilistic outlook, astripperificoutfit, buxom, a gun in each hand, and to top it off, the series takes place in the 1990s. Abusive Parents: Revy's father was a drunk who beat her; judging by her derisive comparison of Greenback Jane to her family services caseworker, it is clear that he was regularly getting reported, but always came shy of getting her taken away from him. Eventually, she murdered him. Amazonian Beauty: She's depicted with muscular biceps at times. Adaptational Angst Upgrade:The idea that she was raped by a police officer is something that is only in the OVA and not from the manga.

characters.name: Benny
characters.description: A Jewish American computer hacker who acts as the Lagoon Company's communications officer and radio operator. Affably Evil: Benny is a pretty decent guy, and would probably be great to have a beer and a few laughs with. His day job involves murder, drug running and grave robbing. Badass Creed: "Fuck the Nazis" is a family motto. He is Jewish, after all (though probably not particularly religious or close to orthodoxy). The Cynic: Benny has no illusions whatsoever about the evils he ignores on a daily basis. He hasn't got Revy's materialistic nihilism, but he's about as cynical as Dutch. As he points to Rock after Gretel gets assassinated:"What do you expect to happen to her? Get cured? Go to school, be happy and make friends? It will never happen and that's just how reality is." Deadpan Snarker: Loves to mock his pals.

characters.name: Dutch
characters.description: A stoic black American veteran of the U.S. Marine Corps and Vietnam War (at least, that's what he says). He is the owner and founder of The Lagoon Company, and the captain of the "Black Lagoon". Adapted Out: TheRoberta's Blood TrailOVA omits the scene whereCaxton tells Benny that Dutch is lying about his service in the Vietnam War, and with it the foreshadowing to theL'homme Sombrearc. Affably Evil: He's the leader of a group of pirates who'll get the job done no matter what it'll take. He's also one of the most sane people of the cast. SeeBenevolent BossandCool Old Guy. Ambiguous Situation:Shane Caxton privately told Benny that he believes that Dutch made up his Vietnam career, as he claimed to have been part of an offensive while serving in a unit that never participated, as well as not knowing basic jargon that anyone who had served would know including the ranks of military officials or any of the guidelines. Later chapters suggest that Dutch did, however, play some sort of role in former French colonies in Africa, particularly Lingani and Zongo's 1989 coup attempt in Burkina Faso as a Colonel known as La Mouche (The Fly). At this point, it's unclear whether Caxton was correct and Dutch is lying (either because he never served in Vietnam, or if he did but was involved in something there that he has good reason to hide), Caxton is mistaken, or if the truth sits somewhere in the middle. Badass Driver: At one point he drives the Lagoon at full speed at a wrecked freighter to use it as a ramp in order to get airborne and shoot a torpedo at a helicopter. Granted, it was Rock's idea, but Dutch deserves kudos for actually pulling it off.

characters.name: In General
characters.description: Former Soviet Special forces soldiers and veterans of the Afghanistan War. Their country turned its back on them and they followed their commander into a life of crime. Badass Crew: Hotel Moscow is comprised of former Special Forces soldiers who have been described as being skilled enough to win World War three. Death Seeker: They all long for the same final battle as Balalaika. The Dreaded: All of Roanapor is terrified of Balalaika and Hotel Moscow. From Camouflage to Criminal: They were all former Special Forces from the Soviet Union. As criminals they're a very tight nit professionally run gang.

characters.name: Sofiya Irininskaya "Balalaika" Pavlovna
characters.description: A former SovietVDVspecial forces commander turned mafia queen; member (along with Mr. Chang and two others) of the four-person commission that regulates crime in Roanapur. Accent Relapse: In the English dub, Balalaika speaks in a refined tone. When she corners Chin and makes clear he will not be surviving the encounter, she switches to her natural Russian accent to demonstrate how annoyed she is. Affably Evil: Balalaika is generally calm, collected, funny, will occasionally spare people's lives on the grounds that they amuse her, is usually willing to negotiate before resorting to violence, and has only lost her temper once in the entire series. However, if negotiations don't go her way, she won't even blink beforecasually gunning down everyone in the room. Alone with the Psycho: Inverted when Balalaika finds herself alone withPsycho for HireHansel. The inversion is thatBalalaikaquite easilyhas him killed. And Your Little Dog, Too!: Balalaika reminds the leaders of the other criminal organisations that herorganisationwill destroy anyone who gets in their way, and their families, and even their pet dog, if necessary.

characters.name: Boris
characters.description: Balalaika's former platoon sergeant during the Soviet-Afghan war, Boris is utterly loyal and devoted to her and is almost always at hisKapitan's side. Affably Evil: His stoicism also comes with a sense of gentlemanly professionalism. He is always respectful to everyone he deals with. Consummate Professional: Boris always remains formal, civil, and businessman like. His interactions with the Lagoon company are always polite and while Balalaika can sometimes indulge in the dramatic, Boris remains quiet and professional. During the Yakuza arc he hides his bloodlust much better than Balalaika does but still casually opines that he wishes they could just kill them all and be done with it. When things get heated with Rock, Boris doesn't hesitate to pull a gun on Revy business relations or no. The Dragon: We can safely assume he is this to Balalaika, despite not having seen him do much so far. It's implied he was her platoon sergeant make in the formal military and he is always at her side speaking with her or delivering orders to the rank-and-file. Even Evil Has Standards: Admits to Balalaika thattaking out Hansel's leg and hand with a sniper rifle and letting him slowly bleed to deathgave him the chills. Though he may have been talking about how he was letting one of the only people to kill a member of the Vysotniki in-series within twenty feet of her.

characters.name: Menshov
characters.description: A Corporal and member of theVysotniki Adaptational Early Appearance: He only shows up to die in the manga but the anime debuts him in episode 9 during Roberta's arc. He reports in on the destruction of Bao's bar as well as revealing to the audience that Bao survived. Cruel and Unusual Death: He's tortured to death by Hansel and Gretel with nails. Friendly Target: The reason he was introduced. Although his death doesn't seem like it was intended to make the audience sad, just horrified. Human Pincushion: Hansel and Gretel tortured him to death by driving nails into his body, most prominently his head. They mention his body was still twitching even after he'd died.

characters.name: Sakharov
characters.description: He is a Private and member of theVysotniki. Friendly Target: The reason he was introduced.Seriously, he didn't even survive the episode he was introduced in.Although his death doesn't seem like it was intended to make the audience sad. Sacrificial Lamb: His introduction to the show is brutally cut short to show that Hansel and Gretel areDead Serious. Said death was whattriggers Hotel Moscow's revenge on Hansel and Gretel.

characters.name: Mr. Chang
characters.description: A former police officer with the Royal Hong Kong Police turned Triad leader; currently engaged in an friendly competition with Balalaika over control of the Roanapur underworld. Affably Evil: A light hearted and mellow crime boss who prefers to conduct business in a peaceful and bloodless fashion and is almost always friendly to everyone he meets. At Least I Admit It: He's a ruthless mob lord, but he makes no bones about what he is and doesn't play at any pretense of justice. Back-to-Back Badasses: He and Revy make an awesome version of this during a gun fight- See the terrorist arc. Badass in a Nice Suit: Chang is a gun-toting Triad boss, clad in a nice suit. He dressed up very fancy when he and Balalaika had their famous duel, while she wore a hell of a dress.

characters.name: Shenhua
characters.description: A Taiwanese assassin in the employ of Mr. Chang. She prefers to use various edged weapons in close combat, in particular a pair of kukri knives linked together with a length of leather rope at the handles, thus using them as modified rope darts. She is also skilled in the use of throwing knives. Affably Evil: Quite cheery most of the time, whether she's skewering haplessMooks, or delivering an unfortunate man in a suitcase to be chopped up by a goth with a chainsaw. She and Revy even have a (relatively) friendly conversation whilst trying to kill each other. Anime Chinese Girl: She speaks in brokenJapanese/Englishwith a heavy accent, wears a qipao and uses cutting weapons and martial arts in a show where most major characters use firearms. Anti-Hero: While she is a skilled assassin and works for a criminal organization, Shenhua also displays acts of kindness and loyalty, particularly towards those she sees as deserving. Likewise, despite her profession, she is portrayed as having a caring side, as Shenhua has been shown to allow Sawyer and Lotton to live with her and even recognized Garcia Lovelace's chivalry. Asian Speekee Engrish: She speaks in broken Japanese and English in both the Japanese and English dubs respectively, something Revy makes fun of whenever they see each other ("Yes lady" in Japanese and "Chinglish" in English).The Italian dub has her be called "liso flitto", so instead of speaking with the r, she speaks with the L.

characters.name: Biu Yuen
characters.description: Chang's most visible assistant, apparently his second-in-command. Beleaguered Assistant: He's introduced with Chang casually tossing his cell phone at him, and further appearances put them into a lighter, more serious version of theComedic Duo. Bodyguarding a Badass: He and the unnamed Triad Mooks who accompany Mr. Chang are armed and ready to defend him, but their boss is easily one of the most dangerous gunfighters in the city. The Comically Serious: With a boss as apparently whimsical asMr. Chang, Biu's appearances tend to cast him as Chang'sStraight Man. The light novel's "Master Ninja" incident comes to mind. Cool Shades: Always wears shades.

characters.name: Eda
characters.description: An easy-going, sunglasses-wearing nun with the so-called Church Of Violence. Revy's confidante and only friend. She is the protagonist ofBlack Lagoon's spinoff mangaEda -Initial Stage-. Badass Boast: Her retort toChang."And another thing, smack talk has no effect on those stronger than you. You and your men have the power to bring men and whole companies to your heels,but we have the power to bring entire nations to our heels, if not to ruin." Batter Up!: At the end ofThe Wired Red Wild Card,while Montero is on a roof with Rock in the sight of his sniper rife, Eda struts up behind him while he's off guard with a Louisville Slugger anddomeshim as hard as she can, causing him to fall to his death to the street below. She does this all while grinning maniacally and listening to the song "Wild Thing" on her Walkman, of course. Beneath the Mask:The ending of the Greenback arc and her role in theEl Baile De La Muertearc indicate that what we see of Eda is mainly a front, and in complete contrast to the bombastic and easygoing drunk she behaves like when on her undercover job, she is actually a cold and calculatingConsummate Professional. Berserk Button: Anyone who puts a bullet in the church had better damn well be prepared to go to war. She doesn't appreciate apprentice priest Rico calling her "sis," either."That's SISTER toyou, jackass!"

characters.name: Sister Yolanda
characters.description: Leader of the Church of Violence. Affably Evil: She seems like just a benevolent, soft spoken elderly lady, aside from the eyepatch. And, you know, the weapons dealing and the drug smuggling. Bling-Bling-BANG!: A gold-plated Desert Eagle. Church Militant: Although it's unclear whether its members are actually religious or are just using the Church as a front, they are still holy scripture reciting, habit wearing, and gun carrying weapons smugglers. Cool Old Lady: Wouldn't it be awesome ifyourgrandma was more like this?

characters.name: Ricardo a.k.a Rico
characters.description: Eda's assistant and a newcomer in the Church Of Violence, who makes his debut in the "Greenback Jane" arc. Forgettable Character: The stunned victim of this in a chapter of the Sawyer spinoff, when Rock and Shenhua appear to not know who he is after he approaches them. With Rock, though, it was just a joke. Shenhua, not so much. More Dakka: His weapons of choice is an M60 Machine Gun. Naïve Newcomer: In the Greenback Jane arc, he's a new member to the Church of Violence. Nice Guy: While he is precisely as violent as the other members of the Church, Rico is very cheerful, introducing himself to Revy and mentioning that "Sis" (Eda) told him a lot about her... all while setting up a bipod-mounted machinegun.

characters.name: Abrego
characters.description: The leader of Roanapur's branch of the Colombian Manisarela Cartel. The Cartel: The Colombian Manisarela. Cluster F-Bomb: Rivals Revy in terms of swearing-to-nonswearing dialogue ratio. Defeat Means Friendship: He mellows down a lot after the end of the "Rasta Blasta" arc. Harmless Villain: Relatively. He's the least threatening of Roanapur's four bosses.

characters.name: Gustavo
characters.description: A high ranking member of the Colombian Manisarela Cartel. Klingon Promotion: He assumes Abrego's position in Roanpur after eliminating him. Mook Lieutenant: A named and characterized minion who wields a level of authority in the Cartel. He lead the detachment searching for Roberta at the start of the "El Baile de la Muerte" arc. Sir Swears-a-Lot: Repeatedly calls Fabiola a puta (whore).

characters.name: Verrocchio
characters.description: Head of an Italian mafia operating in Roanapur. Bad Boss: When an underling suggests they cut their losses by killing the twins and claiming credit for it,Verrocchio brutally beats him, assuming the man wants to usurp him. Bullying a Dragon: Despite having zero combat skill, Verrocchio mouths off to and constantly insults Balalaika. Not only could she crush him like a bug, but this assumes she won't want to pick a fight with the Italian mob for a fun conflict. Even Abrego is more deferential, while Balalaika is thankfully uninterested in breaking the peace. Even worse, he hired Hansel and Gretel to go after Balalaika, which was never going to end well. The Chessmaster: His strategy forknocking out Balalaika involves hiring in outsiders who wouldn't be traced back to him (especially since one of his own "conveniently" dies). Except the outsiders are less-than-subtle spree killers who he can't corral with money or threats. Hate Sink: All of his scenes reinforce him as a violent and unlikeable person; paired against the other three gang leaders he's given the least sympathy. This ends up being his role in the Hansel and Gretel arc, where the twins end up receiving a degree of sympathy from their traumatic backstory while Verrocchio takes the position of the one that the audience is supposed to hate completely.

characters.name: Ronnie "The Jaws"
characters.description: The new leader of the Sicilian mafia faction in Roanapur to replace Verrochio, Ronnie is still a relative unknown but apparently has a dangerous reputation from past work. Cement Shoes: He and his subordinates dispose of someone like this; with Ronnie annoyed that the "aquarium decoration" kept interrupting the conversation he was trying to have until they threw him in the water. Famed in Story: Revy mentions that his faction is considered just as brutal asHotel Moscow. Jerkass: Unlike Balalaika or Chang, who are ruthless gangsters but usually personally affable, Ronnie makes no effort to hide how much of a violent, ruthless scumbag he is.When offering Feng sanctuary and a job at the end of the Wild Red Card arc, he initially offers to shake her hand, but when she approaches, he grabs her by the hair and makes it clear he is the boss and if tries anything funny he'll kill her. Names to Run Away from Really Fast: Is called "The Jaws" thanks to his braces.

characters.name: Chin
characters.description: A minor crime boss in Roanapur until he crosses paths with the Lagoon Company. Asshole Victim: Nobody’s gonna mourn him even with his brutal death. He’s portrayed as nothing but a vile and sleazySmug Snake. Big Bad Wannabe: Wants to be seen as a big crime boss and tries to get Dutch to side with him. It goes as well as you’d expect. Bullying a Dragon: This man,despite being nothing more than a minor criminal, had the sheer balls to go and try and go after one oftheruling crime families in all of Roanapur, an organization explicitly stated to be capable of fightingWorld War IIIand winning, while attacking one of the courier companies allied to said crime family despite having members who pack enough heat to level a small country,and fully expected to get away with it.To compound these delusions, he bragged toeveryonethat he set up Dutch for a trap, meaning Hotel Moscow didn't have to look very hard to snuff him out like a bug.Needless to say, it goes aboutas poorly as you'd expect it to. "Could Have Avoided This!" Plot: Balalaika openly lampshades later to Rock that he could've avoided his rather gruesome fate had he kept low and didn't try to usurp the bigger players; she notes that "even the dead" would've known what he was up to due to his sheer ego.

characters.name: Claude "Torch" Weaver
characters.description: One of theCarnival of Killershired to hunt down Jane in the "Greenback Jane" arc. Acrofatic: While not too major, Claude can move when he needs to and manages to stay on the Lagoon when Dutch rocks it to toss the others off. Even Revy's surprised at how fast he can be though Claude admits that it's taxing on his old bones.Revy: "Got to admit, this guy's pretty quick for a lardass." Affably Evil: Despite being aPsycho for Hirewho likes to burn people with his flamethrower, he seems quite pleasant. Against My Religion: The reason he gives for refusing to touch alcohol, in addition to his aversion toswearing, indicate that he's a Mormon. Beware the Silly Ones: He's a fat Mormon who won't touch booze and maintains a cheerful attitude throughout the entire affair. He is also apyromaniacalmercenary who burns people to death and can give Revy a legit run for her money.

characters.name: Elroy
characters.description: A getaway man known as "Bighorn" Elroy. He's the man you go to if you want to disappear. Boom, Headshot!: When he meetsGretel, he immediately pulls a gun and shoots her in the head. Post-Betrayal Justification:Elroy is paid a tidy sum by Hotel Moscow to kill his newest client Gretel instead of helping her escape. When Dutch asks why he would do this after years of loyally serving his clients, Elroy explains he learned from his daughter-in-law that his son has cancer, so all that matters to him now is fleeing with the bribe and taking care of his family. One Last Job: In a twist on the trope, he reveals this after the job is finished. Villainous Parental Instinct: His son is married in South Africa and had been diagnosed with cancer. Elroydestroys his credibility as a getaway man by breaking a contract and killing the person he was supposed to help because Hotel Moscow paid him off. He chose to retire from his position to go and be with his son.

characters.name: Frederica Sawyer "the Cleaner"
characters.description: A feared presence in the Roanapur underworld, who helps the various crime organizations dispose of corpses (and soon to be corpses) with her trustychainsaw. Actually a rather pretty young goth girl. She is the protagonist ofBlack Lagoon's spinoff mangaSawyer the Cleaner - Dismemberment! Gore Gore Girl. Ax-Crazy: Sawyer loved chopping up people with her chainsaw so much that she became a professional cleaner so she could slice up all the unfortunate people that pissed off the different mafia groups in Roanapur. Badass Adorable: She's capable of fighting people with her chainsaw, to the point she candeflect bullets with it, but at the same time, she's a surprisingly cute, even vulnerable-looking goth-girl. The Butcher: Meat butchering is even her legitimate career, to hide her job as a body-cleaner, torturer-for-hire, and amateur bounty hunter.

characters.name: Leigharch
characters.description: An Irish driver who worked with Shenhua at one time. A compulsive coke fiend (or pot, in the anime), he has a distressingly frequent tendency to hallucinate at inopportune times, such as in the middle of a car chase. Badass Driver: Mixes this withThe Stoner.Shenhua:Even when his head off to Mars, he never mess up driving. Bedlam House: According to Shenhua, he's currently in an asylum due to having taken so much coke that "he never came back from Mars". Bowdlerize: He's on cocaine in the manga, and "merely" on pot in the anime. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: He's an Irish getaway driverwhose car driving skills are completely flawless, even though he drives under the influence of so many drugs that he tends to spend his workday screaming various non-sequiturs about pop culture.Eventually he overdoses and winds up in an institution.

characters.name: Lobos
characters.description: The Neveral Cartel's representative in Roanapur. Unlike Elvis or Russell, he understands how the town works. Affably Evil: Unlike his coworkers, he thinks much more thoroughly and helps stop his gang from committing more harm. In fact, he's only evil because of who he's with. Anti-Villain: He's with the guys trying to kill Jane, but he'll stop things if he feels they go too far. Dirty Coward: What Elvis and Russellthinkhe is because he doesn't want to provoke Hotel Moscow or the Triad. The truth is that they're idiots. The Dog Bites Back:It's strongly implied he kills Elvis at the end of the arc for being an idiot who would have kicked off a gang war.

characters.name: Lotton the Wizard
characters.description: A handsome, long-coated adventurer introduced during the Greenback Jane arc, he is one of the few survivors of the band of mercenaries hunting for Jane. He now lives with the other two, Shenhua and Sawyer the Cleaner. Action Survivor: Basically the only thing he has going for him. He's dumb as a rock and may have more than a few screws loose butsomehowhe manages to not die despite his numerous screw-ups. And in a city like Roanapur, not being dead within your first week of arriving is an achievement in itself. Anti-Villain: He's one of the nicest people in the show, and is only really antagonistic from the viewpoint of the protagonists (and even then, only in his first appearance). Badass on Paper: He's saved a CIA operation that helped stabilize Chinese relations with the U.S, made friends with an actual ninja when said ninja was trying to kill him, got Revy to respect him for being willing to throw down with her, somehow managed to get Eda to follow along with his plans and somehow gained the respect of both Balalaika and Chang. Badass Long Coat: Invoked and subverted. He wears a stylish trenchcoat mostly for dramatic effect... yet he's still laughably ineffectual, despitehis irritating good fortune.

characters.name: Bao
characters.description: Bao is thelong-sufferingowner and bartender of theYellow Flag Bar. His establishment is frequently filled with bullet holes, blown-up, and otherwise trashed, but he always survives by hiding behind his armored bar and firing a shotgun at any threats. Revy owes him for damages, but always manages to avoid paying. He also owns a brothel set up on the top floor of his bar and he is a former ARVN soldier who fought inThe Vietnam War. Bad Guy Bar: The Yellow Flag, naturally. It seems to be the "main" bar of the city and it's where all of the place's criminal factions can meet up at any given time. Balalaika even foots the bill when Roberta blows the place up, indicating that it may be a front for Hotel Moscow (or at the very least is a convenient neutral ground for all of the gangs, considering how many hired guns hang out there). What that means, regarding Bao himself, is anyone's guess. Butt-Monkey:Downplayed. He and his bar have to take a lot of misfortune throughout the series, and it is treated as aRunning Gag, but it's rarely ever targeted at him personally. He just isn't on anyone's radar, and that explains why he's survived for so long. Crazy-Prepared: He's had the bar fortified to stop up to50 caliber bulletsand keeps a semi-automatic shotgun back there too. Deadpan Snarker: Whenever his bar isn't being torn by gunfire or blown up, he shows a snide sense of humor to patrons. When Roberta first visits his bar to find her master Garcia, Bao, assuming that she is a regular maid, bluntly tells her that they don't serve milk here.

characters.name: Rowan "Jackpot" Pigeon
characters.description: Rowan "Jackpot" Pigeon is the owner and manager of theGoofFeststrip club on Rachiada Street in Roanapur. Of African descent, he has offered Revy a job as an S/M dancer more than once, possibly putting her as the role of a dominatrix. He is also a movie dealer who carries both legal and illegal genres (such as all forms of pornography and snuff films). Eating the Eye Candy: Thinks Revy will finally join his brothel during his introduction, asking her if she's "finally gonna make good use of that sweet ass of hers".She eventually does do a BDSM show a few arcs later, but not in earnest as it was only a set-up to smoke out an assassin who was after Lagoon's latest person-of-interest. Harmful to Minors: Dude sells child pornography, and some dialogues imply some of his hookers are underaged. A Lady on Each Arm: Seen with his prostitutes beside him in his introduction, being a pimp and all.

characters.name: Chief Watsap
characters.description: Roanapur's (largely ineffectual) chief of police. Dirty Cop: Lagoon Company pays him off to look the other way when they do business, and later he agrees to keep Hansel and Gretel's killing spree off the record because Balalaika doesn't want the military getting involved. Lack of Empathy: He cares little about maintaining the order of the city to the point he doesn't bat an eye towards criminals like Revy killing people, only expressing concern if they drag his police into their problems. Police Are Useless: The amount of times he can be seen actually doing his job properly can be counted on one hand. He explicitly tells Revy he's fine with her shooting at people, as long as she does it somewhere quiet. Pragmatic Villainy: He reprimands Revy for nearly shooting Rock not out of any morals, but because it is done in a public area, which would mean giving him unnecessary paperwork to fill out.

characters.name: Shane Caxton
characters.description: An US Army Major, and commander of the ISA black-ops unit "Gray Fox" under orders of the NSA - Caxton, like Dutch (supposedly...) is a Vietnam War veteran who has seen the ugly face of both sides, and as a result developed his own moral code and sense of honor, a trait that earns him the absolute respect and obedience of his men. Due to the accidental death of Diego Lovelace during a political assassination for which his unit was responsible for, he unwittingly made an enemy out of Roberta - who effectively declared war on him and the entire NSA. With his next assignment being the capture of Shue Yan, an opium harvester located in the Golden Triangle, Caxton and his men were temporarily stationed in Roanapur to await further orders - and giving Roberta a nice scent. This putallof Roanapur on edge; the Triads, Hotel Moscow, and especially the Cartel given their previous history with her. TheCIAtoo gets involved, due to having a nice fat stake in the opium trade - effectively making the whole ordeal a giant pissing match between the two organizations. As Caxton puts it, he just walked into a "gigantic clusterfuck." Achilles' Heel: His is the fact that he's aFriend to All Children. While it made him a badass during Nam, nowadays it just serves to paint a target on his back - much to the dismay of his men. Affably Evil: To the point where he canhardlyqualify as "evil" at all. He's one of the only few genuinely decent people in the entire series. Artistic License – Military: In a flashback, Caxton is shown to be a lieutenant duringThe Vietnam War. But during the events of the show (over two decades later) he only holds the rank ofmajor. Areal-worldAmerican military officer would hold the rank of at least acolonel(if nothigher) after so many years of service.

characters.name: RayMcDougal
characters.description: Caxton's second in command in the Grey Fox unit. Hero Antagonist: Towards Roberta and the denizens of Roanapur before forming anEnemy Minewith Balalaika and the Lagoon Company to survive Roberta's rampage. Number Two: Shane's second in command, he defers orders down to the men when Shane is busy.

characters.name: Horner
characters.description: A Sergeant Major in the Grey Fox unit. Big Damn Heroes: When Roberta nearly shoots Garcia (thinking he's a hallucination), Horner broke rank to save him and push her back. Friend to All Children: Disobeyed orders to save Garcia. His comrades speculate that he did it because Horner has kids back home. When Garcia pulls a pistol on Shane, Horner tackles and disarms him whereas some of the other foxes pulled their guns. Hero Antagonist: Towards Roberta and the denizens of Roanapur before forming anEnemy Minewith Balalaika and the Lagoon Company to survive Roberta's rampage. Mauve Shirt: One of the foxes with a bit more characterization than the others on account of him saving Garcia.

characters.name: Sanchez
characters.description: The Grey Fox Unit's sharpshooter. Friendly Sniper: An outgoing friendly man and the team sniper. Unlike aCold SniperSanchez works with a spotter to watch his back. Hero Antagonist: Towards Roberta and the denizens of Roanapur before forming anEnemy Minewith Balalaika and the Lagoon Company to survive Roberta's rampage. Impaled with Extreme Prejudice: When Roberta goes around blasting metal bars at the soldiers, he manages to take the impact in his rifle and survive.She throws her musket and impales him on the bayonet. Mauve Shirt: One of the Grey Fox members to get a decent amount of character and dialogue.He's the only significant casualty in the battle with Roberta in the OVA.

characters.name: Sergeant-Major Feng Yifei
characters.description: A hacker for the People's Liberation Army. Her official rank is NCO 5th class, a.k.a. Sgt. Major. Anime Chinese Girl: Interestinglyavertsalmost all the typical stereotypes. She also has a detailed backstory, coming fromShennongjia, Hubei province, and being the granddaughter of a veteran of the Chinese Civil War. Artistic License - Military: The series takes place in the mid-nineties. The rank that can be construed as "Sergeant Major" in the PLA was not created until 2014. A-Team Firing: She gets into a shootout with Revy atpoint blank rangewhile attempting to hijack Rock's car and every shot misses. Except poor Rock who has to contend with all the hot shell casings flying at him. Bilingual Bonus: After Janet smugly reveals how she played her like a fiddle, she furiously yells an untranslated "Ta ma de!" at her ("FUCK YOU!").

characters.name: Colonel Ma
characters.description: Feng's boss back in China. He oversees her operations. Bad Boss: Despite the trope below,he still ordered the assassination of Feng as per his orders from Major General Liu. Benevolent Boss: Made an unauthorized call to Feng after she was "burned" by the PLA to let her know she was on her own and that he would do everything he could to make sure her family was taken care of. The Handler: He was Feng's only point of contact with the PLA. Professional Butt-Kisser: He's mostly concerned with staying on General Liu's good side.

characters.name: Major General Liu
characters.description: Ma's superior officer. Insane Admiral: A general in this case. He liquidates the entire first division after the Germans catch on to the PLA's cyber-espionage activities due to concern it will damage German-Chinese relations. Though it seems so far, the only person slated to be outrightkilledis Feng. Internal Affairs: Operating as this to Colonel Ma's division after the Germans got solid proof they had been compromised by PLA espionage. He Knows Too Much: His suspicions about Feng jump up after it's revealed she knew about the existence of Annenheim Distribution, a PLA shell corporation that was supposed to be above her paygrade. Un-person: After the operation to spy on Rainbach AG is compromised, he orders the complete dissolution of the entire operation, including all peoples associated with it.

characters.name: 2nd Lt. Yeyin
characters.description: General Liu's assistant. Beleaguered Assistant: The poor girl has her hands full trying to run errands for her boss. Only Sane Employee: She sure looks like it, especially when her superiors are having shouting matches with each other. She just tries to stay out of the fight and recite whatever useful information she has. Shrinking Violet: She spends most of her time looking like a deer in the headlights or awkwardly hiding behind her paperwork.

characters.name: Captain Yang
characters.description: A Chinese operative in Roanapur. Contract on the Hitman: Arranges to have Feng killed after she is disavowed by the PLA. Running Gag: Every time he tries to ask the assassin trio he's hired where their fourth brother is, something interrupts him.

characters.name: The Quartet
characters.description: A gang consisting of three men who consider themselves to be brothers, and a mysterious fourth member. They consist of Montero (Afro Brazilian), Robert (Caucasian American) and ParkSeung/Paxon(Korean-American). They were secretly contracted by the PLA to take out Feng to avoid being compromised in the long run. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: All of them have some sort of quirk—Robert is sex crazed and a few hours in a cell next to him while he prattles on is enough to make Revy even more homicidal, Montero constantly quotes the Bible, apparently sincerely despite being a hitman, and Park Seung is dumb but insanely tough. Cold Sniper: Montero.Too bad Rock knows he is a sniper, and has Eda positioned in a place where she could easily dispatch him while he is lining up a shot. Cowboy: Robert makes Russell look restrained in this regard, getting into a gunfight with Revy using a revolver.He manages to stalemate her long enough for police to come and arrest them both. Equal-Opportunity Evil: The Quartet are a gang of criminals from various ethnic/racial backgroundsand both genders.

characters.name: Ginji Matsuzaki
characters.description: Legendary enforcer for the Washimine clan and protector of Yukio Washimine, his skill with a sword is equal to Revy's gunfighting ability. Affably Evil: He's polite, respectful and genuinely cares about Yukio, to where he thanks Rock and Revy for helping him save her. He's also a ruthless Yakuza enforcer who can be very sadistic — as seen with how he taunts and kills the Russian Mafia group — and is willing to do anything for Yukio no matter how amoral or pragmatically questionable it is. Back-to-Back Badasses: Ginji displays synergy with Revy while fighting Chaka's gang at the bowling alley. The Big Guy: Revy calls him "Jumbo" for a reason. He's the biggest and strongest in the Washimine Clan. Blood Knight: He is in vehement denial of his bloodlust for most of the arc, but he embraces it when he slaughters Chaka's men with Revy. When he reaches his final confrontation with Revy,he admits that they aren't that differentand doesn't even try to deny his love of combat for their final duel.

characters.name: Yukio Washimine
characters.description: A high school girl andheir to the Washimine Clan, who takes over leadership of the group when it's at war with Balalaika and the old one, Tsugio Bandou, loses his life. Adaptational Badass: In the anime, while exhibiting the same flaws and insecurities as in the manga, Yukio takes on a more active role in combating Hotel Moscow, working with Ginji to frame the Hotel Moscow for a bank robbery and staging Rock's kidnapping, and has a more defined goal in going to Roanapur to rebuild her clan. Affably Evil: She’s rather pleasant and polite towards Rock in each of their conversations and has a cordial relationship with Ginji and herYakuzasubordinates. The only reason she is evil because she is a part of and becomes the head of the Yakuza. She doesn’t prove to be a big threat on her own, though. Anti-Villain: She is one of the few honorable and ethical people in the series just happens to be antagonistic to the viewpoint characters. She chooses to become ayakuzaboss when Balalaika kills the previous one, since she's next in line. Better to Die than Be Killed: She chooses todie by her own hand, either to avert being at the mercy of rival clans or Hotel Moscow, preserve her honor like an oldschoolYamato Nadeshikowould, orto be with Ginjior a mix of all three.

characters.name: Chaka
characters.description: One of the Washimine family'senforcerswho attempted to take control of the family. 0% Approval Rating: None of his subordinates like him because he's such a horribleBad Bossto the point that they even turn against him. Amazon Chaser: Revy being dangerous and violent is ahugeturn-on for him.Chaka: You're the one I've been waiting to meet, Revy. Truth is, I've never met a lady gunman before, and now, here we are together. I wanna fuck you, Revy.Revy: I make it a point never to fuck assholes. Or pussies. An Arm and a Leg: When Chaka goads Ginji into drawing his sword, Ginji cuts off his hands before he drowns him in a swimming pool. Ax-Crazy:Deconstructed. Underneath the thin layer of fake bravado, Chaka is aPsychopathic Manchildwhose cruelty, love of violence, and lust for battle all define him. However, this ends up being a detriment to himself, as his poor impulse control and gratuitous cruelty ends up alienating him from his formerYakuzapeers and his own gang, eventually leading to his undoing.

characters.name: Tsugio Bandou
characters.description: Yukio's immediate predecessor as the leader of the Washimine clan, and a friend of her late father Ryuzou. By the time he took charge, the clan was already in danger of being absorbed by a larger and more powerful rival. He resorts to contacting the Russian mafia for help, leading to the events of the story arc. Defiant to the End: He attacks Balalaika with a dagger and is still violently struggling in her arms before she kills him. Even Evil Has Standards: For him, the final straw came when Balalaika proposed kidnapping the rival clan leader's family members. Face Death with Dignity: As the situation with the Russians breaks down, he goes for one final meeting, fully believing that he won't make it back. He tells Yoshida that they must listen to Ginji now, and that he's a good man. Failure Is the Only Option: In the end, he is left with two equally undesirable choices: either continue cooperating with Hotel Moscow and have every otheryakuzaclan in Japan turn against the Washimine clan, or cut ties with their erstwhile ally and incur the wrath of the mafia.

characters.name: Yoshida
characters.description: Tsugio's bodyguard, and later one of Yukio's supporters in the Yakuza. Affably Evil: While he is part of the Yakuza, Yoshida is a loyal and devoted man who regards his boss Bandou as an older brother and is supportive towards Yukio when she becomes the leader of the clan following Bandou's death. Boom, Headshot!: When a wounded Yoshida holds on to Chaka to give time for Yukio to escape, Chaka finishes him off by putting a cap on his head. Even Evil Has Standards: Chaka's disrespect for the clan's authority and their guests ticks him off. When he sees Chaka beating Rock up, Yoshida slams him against the wall and calls him a disgrace. Heroic Sacrifice: A villainous example. After being shot by Chaka, he attempts to hold down and distract him while Yukio runs off. Sadly, it doesn't work and she ends up being violently beaten by one of Chaka's men right after Yoshida is murdered.

characters.name: Maki
characters.description: Maki is a high-school junior who goes to the same school as Yukio. She's not involved with the Yakuza in any way at all. Instead, she's an average Japanese high school girl who looks up to Yukio as her sempai. Foil: To Yukio, showing what shemighthave been if she were born in a normal family. Girlish Pigtails: She wears her hair in two cute tails, contrasting with her more mature friend Yukio, who has her long hair untied. Naïve Everygirl: She is quite unaware of Yukio's background and wouldn't imagine a girl her age would be put in charge of a Yakuza family. Satellite Character: Much of her characterization revolves around her interactions with Yukio, only appearing to provide insight on Yukio's personal life. When Yukio abandons her normal life to become the clan's leader, Maki disappears from the plot entirely.

characters.name: Hanada
characters.description: One of Chaka's goons who has a very short temper. Batter Up!: While engaging both Revy and Ginji in the anime, Hanada briefly swings a baseball bat at the former, only to miss and get killed by the latter for his troubles. Dies Differently in the Adaptation: In the manga, Hanada is among the hiding gang members who then try to flee when Revy finds them before gunning all of them down. The anime instead has him get cut down by Ginji. Dirty Coward: In the manga, he not only pleads with Chaka for mercy as he's beaten up for disobeying him, but he also hides during the gunfight and then tries to run away rather than face Revy, in contrast to his anime counterpart, who at least tries to fight her head on. Disproportionate Retribution: In response to being bumped into by Yukio, Hanada viciously batters her to near-death, only being stopped from going any further by Chaka.

characters.name: Okazaki
characters.description: One of Chaka's goons who joins in with him on a twisted strip game with Yukio as the victim. Dies Differently in the Adaptation: While he's still killed by Revy in both the manga and anime, in the former, another henchman got his death scene while Okazaki was one of the goons trying to run away from her before being gunned down, even being the last one she kills as he fearfully looks up at her. Dirty Coward: His smug sadism goes out the window when Revy shoots up most of the gang and he's left trying to beg her to spare him, getting more increasingly panicked when he realizes that's not going to happened. In the manga, he's one of Chaka's men who initially hides from Revy during the gunfight and then fearfully tries to run away from her as she mocks the group before shooting them all. Face Death with Despair: Once Revy has him at gunpoint after she and Ginji massacre most of Chaka's gang, Okazaki dies either looking up at her in fear (in the manga) or pathetically begging for his life (in the anime). Hate Sink: Like all of the members of Chaka's gang, Okazaki is a depraved, smugJerkasswho gleefully takes part in forcefully stripping Yukio as part of a twisted bowling game all while enjoying her suffering.

characters.name: Roberta
characters.description: A maid who worked for four years at the Lovelace household in Venezuela. Although her domestic skills such as cleaning and cooking were somewhat lacking, she developed a close friendship with the young son of the Lovelace family, Garcia. Roberta was once known as Rosarita Cisneros, a former FARC guerrilla trained as an assassin in Cuba and an internationally wanted criminal. She was taken in by the Lovelaces to clear a debt of honor between Roberta's father and the head of the family, who then became her master. Abnormal Ammo: Using ametal rod that is capable of penetrating armorisn't what is expected for acenturies-old musketto fire.To be fair, musketscanfire flechettes with some minor tweaking, which is precisely what she requests a gunsmith in Roanapur to do. To be fair, musketscanfire flechettes with some minor tweaking, which is precisely what she requests a gunsmith in Roanapur to do. The Ace: Roberta is perhaps the series' best overall combatant, able to take on multiple seasoned combatantson her own. In the ''Dance of Death" arc, it took three elite combat groups to finally slow her down. Adaptational Karma: In the manga version ofRoberta's Blood Trail,she gets to return home without a scratch on her after slaughtering Caxton's men. In the OVA adaptation, she gets to go home minusseveral limbsandan eye.

characters.name: Garcia Fernando Lovelace
characters.description: The young son of Roberta's master Diego, heir to the Lovelace family. When he's kidnapped and later the Lagoon company gets the work of "transporting" him, Roberta goes against our "heroes" to get herMorality Chainback. All-Loving Hero: Stubbornly refuses to resort to violence as a means to an end,knowing the consequences of it. He also keeps Fabiola from making this mistake.The one time he appears to subvert this, it was a ruse. Break the Cutie:Vehemently defied. During the entirety ofEl Baile de la Muerte, the poor boy is tormented and given several chances toJump Off The Slippery Slope, but he never breaks completely and is deadset on bringing Roberta back to her old self with a minimum of bloodshed. Chekhov's Gunman:Gun included, albeit unloaded; he only fires blanks with it, in a gambit to stop Roberta'sRoaring Rampage of Revengewithout killing any more people. It works. A Child Shall Lead Them:Becomes the Lovelace family head out of necessity after his father is killed.

characters.name: Diego Jose San Fernando Lovelace
characters.description: Garcia's father, Roberta's boss and leader of the Lovelace family. Whose tragic death kicks off theEl Baile de la Muertearc. Class Traitor: He is of the old landowning class in Venezuela (well known for their right-wing politics), but when he was killed he was participating in a meeting of Hugo Chavez' fledgeling Fifth Republic Movement - which was even then socialism-inclined. Disappeared Dad: More like blown to smithereens, but still… Impoverished Patrician: According to Rock, the Lovelace family is on the lower rungs of Venezuelan high society. While he still has quite a bit of money due to plantations, it's still not much compared to what the Lovelaces used to have in the past. This is due to Diego's political beliefs (he's a quasi-socialist amongst a famously capitalist group) and the harrassment of the Colombian cartel. Morality Chain: Roberta owes him her new chance at life, and thus she goes batshit when he kicks it.

characters.name: Fabiola Iglesias
characters.description: Another maid in the Lovelace household, and the only one who's trained in hand-to-hand combat and weaponry like Roberta. After she leaves in herRoaring Rampage of Revenge, Fabiola becomes Garcia's caretaker. Abusive Parents: She looks up to her parents as honest hard working people. She states that when she stole a CD player for her younger brother that her mother beat her black and blue for it. Revy says that sounds like abuse to her but Fabiola insists that her mother did it out of love. Action Girl: One of the very few female warriors in the series that aren't considerablydarker. Awesomeness by Analysis: She learned Capoeira from watching people practice. No formal training involved. Badass Adorable: Basically Roberta Lite.

characters.name: Alfredo Caramasa
characters.description: A Cuban special forces operative, hired by the FARC to capture or kill Rosarita Cisneros/Roberta during her rampage in Roanapur - and with good reason, this man isskilled enough to take her on.He knows a lot about her past, though Roberta herself does not recognize him. Amazon Chaser: He has a thing for Roberta, allowing her to undress when she pretends to offer him sex. However, this isn't enough for him to lower his gun, as he suspects that Roberta may something under her sleeve. Badass Normal: He is a seemingly normal soldier who is Roberta's equal and briefly has the upper hand on her in a fight. Charles Atlas Superpower: During their brief scuffle, he can blockRobertablow for blow, and punch hard enough to make her vomit, whereas a car crash didn't leave a scratch on her. Didn't See That Coming: He doesn't drop his guard around Roberta for even a split second, but he didn't expect her to have a derringer hidden in her belt buckle - it cost him.

characters.name: Ibraha
characters.description: A Middle-Eastern terrorist and member of the PLO who's in Basilan. His path crosses the Lagoon Company's when they're tasked with delivery of insider info on his group's next target. Arc Villain: He along with his co-commander Takenaka serve as the main antagonists of the "Goat, Jihad and Rock 'n Roll" arc, with both of them seeking to take the documents from the Lagoon Company. Detrimental Determination: Ibraha is willing to take extreme risks to achieve his goals, no matter how damaging the consequences.His inability to concede the battle in front of him gets him killed by his own comrade Takenaka. Middle Eastern Terrorists: Made more explicit in the manga, where he'sexplicitlyaffiliated with theLebanese Hezbollah. The anime instead changes the name of his affiliation to the Protectors of the Islamic Front. Motive Rant: When the Lagoon crew is about to reach the military camp, Takenaka tries to make Ibraha break off the chase by appealing to his dead son. Ibraha breaks down and begins ranting about how he can never stop because of what Israel and its allies did to him.

characters.name: Masahiro Takenaka
characters.description: A political terrorist and member of the Japanese Red Army who runs afoul of the Lagoon Company during their delivery on insider info of a middle-eastern terrorist group he's allied with. Affably Evil: Seems completely genuine in his friendliness. Arc Villain: He along with his co-commander Ibraha serve as the main antagonists of the "Goat, Jihad and Rock 'n Roll" arc, with both of them seeking to take the documents from the Lagoon Company. Card-Carrying Villain: He is a tragic and self-aware take on this. Once a member of the Japanese Red Army, he's long lost any hope of bringing about a Communist revolution and associates with terrorist groups that have nothing to do with his old politics. He describes himself as an enemy of the state by profession, since being a public menace is the only thing that gives his life any meaning. Chummy Commies: Manages to play both this andDirty Communists, as while he is an antagonist, his dedication to communismnoteimplied to be specificallyTrotskyismgiven his use of the phrase "permanent worldwide revolution" and theReal LifeRed Army being Trotskyistis treated sympathetically, and he shows a fair bitmorehonor and concern for his men than many of the protagonists' allies.

characters.name: Elvis
characters.description: Leader of the Neveral Cartel in Florida. Hired Jane and her group to counterfeit money for them, only for her to escape after he kills their network administrator. Is unfamiliar with Roanapur, and in over his head. Bad Boss: The whole reason Jane ran away is his mistreatment of his employees. While her team ran overbudget and past multiple deadlines, he still immediately decides to kill a member of her team in response, ignorant of his victim's importance to the project. Bullying the Dragon: Rather quickly pisses off Revy and the Rip Off Church, and it only gets worse from there. Establishing Character Moment: His introductory scene has him stupidly gun down one of Jane's colleagues while threatening her when her team misses the deadline, despite the fact that he needs them to counterfeit money for his gang in the first place, resulting in Jane being left with less manpower and escaping to the Rip-Off Church for protection. This shows that Elvis is an impulsive and egotistical hotshot who makes a blunder too many without considering the consequences. Fish Out of Water: He is unprepared for the simmering cesspit that is Roanapur. He really wants to go back to Florida.

characters.name: "Groovy" Guy Russell
characters.description: The Florida cartel's "trouble buster" who leads the group hired to go after Jane. Bounty Hunter: The leader of the RoanapurCarnival of Killers. Butt-Monkey: Even the peoplehe hirestreat him like garbage and refuse to obey him. Ironically, he ends upoutliving most of them. Cowboy: He's either one completely or just affecting airs to be cool. Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: Is treated like a totalButt-Monkeyfrom his first entrance, and his obnoxious and bossy attitude doesn't help him live this down. All said and done, other than Shenhua he's also the deadliest and most competent of the bunch.

characters.name: Alfred
characters.description: An SS Officer that hired the Lagoon Company to retrieve a lost painting from a sunken U-boat. Evil Old Folks: He is an elderly man who is nonetheless a genocidal, racist Nazi. Faux Affably Evil: He is initially polite to Dutch, but it’s clear that he is still a Nazi that holds on to his racist ideology. Playing Both Sides: He pitted both Rachmann and the Aryan Socialist Union against the Lagoon Company as a test to see if they were worth his support. Politically Incorrect Villain: As a Nazi war criminal, he holds all other races in contempt and considers them to be inferior.

characters.name: E.O. Captain
characters.description: The sadistic leader of the Extra Order Company, a mercenary group hired by Kageyama to kill the Lagoon Company and prevent them from giving the disc to Hotel Moscow. Ax-Crazy: He is a bloodthirsty and trigger-happy mercenary who uses his job to slaughter as many people as he can, even those he isn't paid to gun down. The Heavy: While Kageyama serves as the prologue's main antagonist, the captain is the one who takes direct action in going after the Lagoon Company, using the resources given by his boss in his attempts to kill them. Leave No Survivors: He orders every target slaughtered, noting "if there's one thing I hate, it's survivors." Revy notes it's a great line before she starts fighting back. More Despicable Minion: While his boss Kageyama is aCorrupt Corporate Executive, the captain is much worse than him, being a unhinged and sadisticPsycho for Hirewho murdered elderly and children alike back when he was part of the military and tries to murder everyone in his way during his pursuit of the Lagoon Company.

characters.name: Hansel and Gretel
characters.description: A pair of incestuous, prepubescent porn star assassins with shared multiple personality disorders. Creepy as Hell. And just as horribly broken due to their horrendous common backstory. They arrive in Roanapur as part of a scheme by the local branch of the Italian Mafia, but things quickly spiral out of control. Advertised Extra: Though they appear only in one arc, theirpopularityled to the twins appearing in advertising and merchandise. Alas, Poor Villain: While they certainly deserved it, their deaths are no less tragic.Hansel is treated to a slow death, and his reaction to bleeding out is to cry like any normal child would. Gretel on the other hand is unceremoniously killed after being shown kindness for the first in her life time; she dies staring at the sunshine she had been deprived of for a long time. Ambiguous Gender:They both have short hair and swap a wig and voices, taking turns being the boy and the girl. As a result, despite appearing to beHalf-Identical Twinsmost of the time, it's left unclear what genders they really are. Parodied in an omake where all the characters changed genders… and they still looked exactly the same. An Arm and a Leg:Hansel getsknee-cappedby a sniper during his encounter with Balalaika, then he gets his forearm blasted off by a second sniper when he tries to throw his axe at Balalaika.

characters.name: Janet "Greenback Jane" Bhai
characters.description: An Indian counterfeiter whose goal is to create perfect counterfeit money. After members of the Floridian cartel that hired her lose patience with her due to continuedschedule slipsand shoot one of her co-workers to death before giving her a 48-hours deadline to finish her job, she flees from the members of the cartel and eventually seeks sanctuary with the Church of Violence, unleashing amadpursuit. The Big Damn Kiss: Gives one to Benny during the closing stages of her introductory arc, after he hacked into her dead associate's database to retrieve some important files for her counterfeiting scheme. Butt-Monkey: Her first time in Roanapur sucked incredibly hard. Her colleague gets shot and she has to run from a cartel. Jane goes to the Ripoff Church for sanctuary, and gets ripped off by Eda. Eda then betrays her to many contract killers to get more money. Jane gets a little rest in a bad motel, then gets chased by abunch of madmenthe rest of the night. And Eda kept extorting more and more cash from the unfortunate sod, too. Comically Missing the Point: Benny warns her that if they rent Mr. Bao's room to spend the night, they'll be main characters in an involuntary porn movie. Her reaction is to demand Bao to give her the room for free. Extreme Libido: She returns to Roanapur as a "grade-A fuck freak" (as Revy puts it) willing to have sex with Benny while he's driving or even when they're in front of a surveillance camera. Benny doesn't seem to care though, or at the very least is too flustered by her hyper-sexual behavior to say anything.

characters.name: Le Cinq Doigts
characters.description: A group of five girls working forDGSE. They are looking for a specific black man and are asking any black men about a certain date. Badass in a Nice Suit: All of them wear black suits, and can go toe-to-toe with local bruisers. Aside from being stylish, the suits are armored—allowing them to survive shots from Revy's cutlasses or slashes from Shenhua's kukri. Boom, Headshot!:How L'index and L'auriculaire die, by Balalaika and Revy respectively. Bullying the Dragon:Unfortunately on the receiving end of this after killing two of Balalaika's men during their rampage through Roanapur, thinking they will muscle their way around the city. Coupled with Le Majeur'srightful retaliationfor their betrayal, the remainder of the group isswiftly eliminatedby Hotel Moscow.They quickly decide toretreat and regroupupon encountering Shenhua and Revy during their mission—despite numbers and bulletproof gear they are on the backfoot almost immediately. They quickly decide toretreat and regroupupon encountering Shenhua and Revy during their mission—despite numbers and bulletproof gear they are on the backfoot almost immediately.

characters.name: Los Soldados
characters.description: Also known as Los Eses, they are an emerging paramilitary group that joined with the Nuevo Laredo cartel, being the focus of theEl Réquiem De Los Desalmadosarc. They have a bone to pick with Hotel Moscow for the losses inflicted upon them by a Vysotniki group supporting a rival cartel in California, demanding the head of the Hotel Moscow leader responsible, otherwise they would take it themselves. They are led by Edgardo PrudencioGris El TigresEscarpa. Blood Knight: Gris and his men are nothing but enthusiastic and hyped that they would be taking on the whole of Roanapur and Hotel Moscow, which they modeled their group after. The Cartel: While they are the Nuevo Laredo cartel's muscle, they themselves started as one when they began growing in power and influence, dealing drugs, running a protection racket and crushing rival cartels. Demanding Their Head: They arrived in Roanapur demanding the head of Hotel Moscow's Vasily Krivchenko for the losses inflicted by Hotel Moscow's support of a rival cartel against them. Refusing diplomatic compromises to avoid looking weak, they declare war on Hotel Moscow to take it themselves, plunging the city into chaos. Fallen Hero: Once vigilantes protecting their impoverished town that was neglected by the authorities from criminals, they became criminals themselves to fund their activities and growing influence among other towns, as the towns they protected were too poor to fund them. While they are still well regarded at home, they are a fearsome cartel hit squad and drug dealers everywhere else.

characters.name: Vasily Laptev
characters.description: The head of Hotel Moscow's Japanese division, and an ex-KGBagent. He does not get along with Balalaika. Bad Boss: When one of his men cannot contact Balalaika (because she is ducking his calls) and advises him to contact his superiors, Vasily stabs the man's hand. Dirty Coward: He begs for his life as Ginji approaches him. It doesn't work, and Ginji executes him. Former Regime Personnel: After the Soviet Union collapsed, he left theKGBand became a criminal.

characters.name: Revy's Father
characters.description: Revy'sAbusive Dad, who's long dead by the start of the series. Abusive Parents: He regularly beat up Revy when she was younger, which often got him in trouble. His apparent lack of care thathis daughter was raped by a policemanin the OVA is what led to her killing him. Alcoholic Parent: Revy regularly talks about how he sent her to get booze when she was younger. The Ghost: Revy talks about him a lot, yet we never see him besides in the OVA. Hate Sink: Despite being long dead, he is anAbusive Dadwho is responsible for many of Revy's issues in the story. Along with regularly assaulting and insulting Revy during her childhood, he cared more about getting drunk than looking after for his daughter. His apathy towardsRevy being arrested, beaten, and raped by aDirty Copproves to be the last straw for her, prompting her to murder him.

characters.name: The Okajimas
characters.description: Rock's neglectful family, whom consists of his parents and at least an older brother. The Ghost: We hear about them only once. When Revy encourages Rock to see his family whilst in Japan, he reveals he's estranged from them. Parental Favoritism: When Rock failed to get into college the first time, they gave up on him and turned their attention to his smarter older brother, who ended up working for the Japanese government. Parental Neglect: Rock mentions they wanted him to reach a certain college. By the time he did, his brother had done more. Small Role, Big Impact: They are only mentioned, but they also likely contributed to Rock sticking around in Roanapur.

characters.name: Kageyama
characters.description: Rock's boss at his old job. Bad Boss: He was willing to throw Rock under the bus and deem him dead. Rock later implies in his conversation with Revy that his boss didn't treat him any better before he was kidnapped. Hate Sink: Besides a sole literalPet the Dogmoment in the anime, Kageyama is a cold, heartlessCorrupt Corporate Executivewho is uncaring towards his employees, such as declaring Rock to be dead when he is kidnapped by the Lagoon Company and endangering him by sending a group of bloodthirsty mercenaries after him and the group. This abuse proves to be the last straw for Rock, who decides to resign from his former job and join the Lagoon Company. Karma Houdini: He gets out mildly inconvenienced as he still gets to go home and retain his job. Parental Neglect: His last scene in the anime shows he's not really a family man, only really caring for his dog.
